scope: P3-HAIL-20 semantics; no runtime or public-contract change

multi_hazard_problem.consequence: hail evidence can exist in an event whose primary hazard_type is severe_thunderstorm
multi_hazard_problem.semantic_decision: primary hazard_type must not be treated as the complete set of event hazard semantics

explicit_event.meaning: hail is explicitly named in primary provider event labeling

contextual_text.meaning: hail is mentioned only in contextual provider text

dwd.rule: real official event content must support hail; registry/topic metadata alone is not an active hail event

noaa_nws.rule: event/headline versus description/instruction evidence should remain distinguishable

invariants: Official hail alert is not observed hail.
Severe thunderstorm is not automatically hail.
Hail evidence must not be considered absent solely because another primary hazard label matched first.
Radar hail signature is not observed hail.
Radar reflectivity alone is not hail proof.
Hail probability is not official warning.
Missing hail size is not invented.
Missing alert stage is not invented.
Provider ID is not a scoring axis.
Private extensions remain outside the standard core contract.
decisions_for_p3_hail_30: Decide whether weather.warning.official remains the broad official hail transport without a new public ID.
Decide how official_hail_alert_event is represented additively.
Decide how explicit_event and contextual_text hail evidence are represented.
Decide whether existing alert_stage is reused for hail.
Preserve hail evidence even when primary hazard_type is severe_thunderstorm.
Keep observed hail, hail size, radar hail signature and probability outside the warning contract.
